text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGE FIRED - AUTH-JWT-KEYMISMATCH (severity: P1) - token validation failures spike across auth-service (500s/401s). Root service: auth-service. Pager: escalation to oncall:sre. thread_ts=1769800123

pagerduty: Automated escalation: primary oncall paged (carla). Please acknowledge.

carla (sre-oncall): acked. I'm on it. seeing 401 spike in prod auth metrics. link: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/auth-jwt?from=-5m to=now

mark (backend): noticed a deploy 8m ago to auth-service that updated JWKS push. Error rate jumped immediately after. Logs show "no matching kid" in token header.

hamid (security): can confirm token signatures failing validation against current JWKS. suspicious that the new key wasn't published to jwks endpoint or kid mismatch.

elena (support): customers reporting login failures and API key operations failing. Support queue filling up; flagging high customer impact.

sasha (infra): pulling recent deploys and config: deploy id 2026-03-14-9463 by ci-bot. JWKS endpoint returned 502 for ~30s during rollout. cache TTL is 1m.

carla (sre-oncall): mitigation plan: 1) revert the deploy if safe, 2) if not, patch auth-service to accept previous key until JWKS back-propagates, 3) inform customers. I'm going to try restarting the auth instances to force JWKS refresh.

mark (backend): adding quick debug output to auth: printing token header, kid, and keys found. snippet:```json
{"kid":"k_2026_03_new","alg":"RS256"}
```

mark (backend): JWKS endpoint currently returns keys: ["k_2026_03_old"]. new key not present. looks like CI pushed key to secrets manager but the publish-to-jwks job failed.

carla (sre-oncall): rolled restart of auth-service (canary) now. curl health:```bash
curl -v https://auth.internal/_health
```

deploy-bot: Canary restart completed for auth-service instance i-0a1b2c3d.

carla (sre-oncall): monitoring error rate... still high on canary but slightly lower. hitting all instances restart next.

hamid (security): quick temporary mitigation: we can accept previous key if we allow both kids for validation. Mark, can you hotfix auth to fallback to cached key if jwks fetch fails?

mark (backend): pushing hotfix to auth-service to consult a local cached jwks file and accept both kids for 10m. patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pulls/4123 - deploying now.

carla (sre-oncall): deploying hotfix to prod with gradual rollout. If successful we'll clear most 401s.

elena (support): posting customer-facing note: "We are experiencing authentication errors; our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes."

sasha (infra): looks like the publish job to jwks bucket failed with permission denied on the service account. error from publish job logs: ```bash
PermissionError: 403: iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob not allowed
```

hamid (security): that matches: new key wasn't published because signing service lost permission after a recent IAM cleanup. Contacting cloud-ops to restore permission.

carla (sre-oncall): hotfix is rolling, I'm seeing 401s drop from 24% -> 6% over 4 minutes. continuing rollout.

mark (backend): hotfix accepted by 90% of instances. JWKS now contains both old and new keys in the local cache on instances. Validation errors almost gone.

pagerduty: Alert suppressed after ack by carla. Auto-escalation paused.

carla (sre-oncall): initiating customer impact assessment: affected tenants: hosted-api customers in us-east-1 using session tokens. Estimate: ~12% of auth calls returned 401s during incident window. Potential duration ~8 minutes from deploy to mitigation.

elena (support): preparing postmortem customer email draft. will wait for final impact numbers.

sasha (infra): cloud-ops confirmed IAM permission restored to signing job at 1769800400. publish job retried and JWKS endpoint now shows both keys properly.

mark (backend): rolling back the hotfix is safe now; I'll remove the fallback after 30 minutes to validate no regression. plan: remove fallback, keep monitoring.

carla (sre-oncall): marking incident as mitigated. status: customers affected briefly, keys propagation failure due to IAM permission change during key publish. root cause: permission regression on signing job + tight jwks-cache window.

deploy-bot: Canary: removal of fallback scheduled.

carla (sre-oncall): handing off to sasha for post-incident monitoring and postmortem coordination. sasha, you're up for the handoff — see notes above.

sasha (infra): taking over. I'll run the incident checklist, collect graphs, logs, and open a postmortem doc. postmortem link: https://docs.internal/postmortems/auth-jwt-1769800123

hamid (security): action items I'm tracking: 1) ensure signing job IAM policy includes required permissions and is covered by integration tests, 2) audit last 30 days of IAM changes.

mark (backend): action items: 1) increase jwks-cache TTL to 5m temporarily, 2) add CI job that validates jwks publish step on key rotation.

elena (support): action items: prepare customer comms and triage any high-severity support tickets created during the window.

carla (sre-oncall): final note: severity lowered to P2 for postmortem. Will include timeline and mitigation steps in the doc. Good work everyone. :white_check_mark:

sasha (infra): confirmed no new regression at 1769800710. closing active paging thread. we will follow up in the postmortem doc with exact metrics and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident incident-1769800123: MITIGATED. Runbook run: auth-jwt-key-rotation.
